title: Test cart actions as pure transitions
summary: Implement cart actions as pure transitions, then design tests for duplicate SKUs, removal, clearing, and mutation bugs.

scenario.briefing: The cart grows a duplicate row every time the same product is added. The team wants the update logic tested before the store is wired into more screens.

objectives.description: Implement cart actions without mutating the current array.
Select the test cases that cover real cart behavior.

hints: Find an existing line by SKU before adding a new one.
Merge a duplicate by returning a new array with an increased quantity.
Removing and clearing return filtered or empty arrays.
Never call push or sort on the incoming array.

misconceptions.description: Appending a second row for the same SKU.
misconceptions.testDescription: Adding the same SKU increases its quantity.
misconceptions.feedback: A cart has one row per SKU. Merge quantities when the SKU already exists so totals and removal stay correct.

misconceptions.description: Mutating the current array in place.
misconceptions.testDescription: Removing a SKU returns a new array.
misconceptions.feedback: A signal only notifies when it receives a different value. Return a new array from every action.

misconceptions.description: Testing rendered markup instead of transitions.
misconceptions.feedback: Markup snapshots do not prove merge or removal behavior. Test the reducer with explicit starting arrays and actions.

sections.title: Stores update through functions
sections.body: A cart store should expose actions that return the next array. Merging a duplicate SKU and removing the last unit are transitions, not mutations of the current array.

sections.title: Test the transition
sections.body: Call the reducer with a starting array and an action, then assert the returned array. Testing the signal wrapper adds noise without proving the update logic.

sections.title: Name the risky cases
sections.body: Duplicate SKUs, removal of the last unit, clearing, and unknown actions are the cases that break a cart. A happy-path test that only adds one row misses them.

vocabulary.definition: A plain object that describes an update to a store.
A function that returns the next state for an action.
Returning a new array instead of changing the current one.

steps.title: Reduce cart actions
steps.prompt: Edit cartStore.ts. Implement add, remove, and clear. Merge duplicate SKUs, return new arrays, and leave the input untouched.
hints: Use a switch on action.type and handle every action explicitly.
For add, search for a line with the same SKU.
For a duplicate, map the array and increase only that line's quantity.
For remove, filter by SKU; for clear, return a new empty array.

steps.title: Design the cart tests
steps.prompt: Select every case the cart reducer needs. Leave out cases that assert the wrong behavior.
hints: Cover merge, remove, clear, and an unknown action.
Think about the input array after the call.
Reject assertions that require mutation or rendered HTML.
Keep cases that describe the reducer contract.

cases.label: Adding an existing SKU increases its quantity.
Removing the last unit drops the line.
An unknown action leaves the array unchanged.
Asserts that the original array was mutated in place.
Compares the rendered store output as an HTML string.

steps.explanation: The reducer contract covers merge, remove, clear, and an unknown action that returns the same array. Mutation is the bug, and HTML snapshots do not exercise the reducer.
